CARLOS2ESTIRIA.name: Charles II, Archduke of Inner Austria
CARLOS2ESTIRIA.summary: Son of Emperor Fernando I, archduke of Inner Austria since 1564. His son Fernando II took this branch of Styria to the imperial throne.

governmentNotes.Gobernó Estiria, Carintia y Carniola des: He ruled Styria, Carintia and Carniola from Graz after his partition from 1564.

ISABPORTEMP.name: Isabella of Portugal
ISABPORTEMP.summary: Daughter of Manuel I of Portugal and Maria of Aragon, married her cousin Charles V in Seville in 1526. She ruled Castile during the Emperor's absences and died in Toledo in 1539, after a difficult birth; he was the mother of Philip II.

PETER1CYPRUS.name: Peter I of Cyprus
PETER1CYPRUS.summary: He promoted expeditions against the Muslim powers of the Eastern Mediterranean and sought support in European courts. The seizure and looting of Alexandria in 1365 did not result in a lasting conquest. His murder opened a crisis within the Cypriot court.

governmentNotes.Título dinástico sin dominio territorial: Dynastic title without territorial rule over Jerusalem.

GASTON3FEBUS.name: Gaston III, Count of Foix
GASTON3FEBUS.summary: Count of Foix and Viscount of Béarn, known as Gaston Fébus, he ruled a patrimony of great importance in the Pyrenees. His marriage to Agnes of Navarre connected him to the House of Évreux.
GASTON3FEBUS.biography: Count of Foix and Viscount of Béarn, known as Gaston Fébus, he ruled an important Pyrenean inheritance. His marriage to Agnes of Navarre connected him with the House of Évreux. The death of his son Gaston left the succession to a collateral branch, making Matthew and Isabella of Castellbó essential to the later history of his house.

governmentNotes.La muerte de su hijo Gastón precedió a l: The death of his son Gaston preceded his count's. The continuity passed through a collateral branch, and did not pass through a offspring of his successor Mateo.

FRANCOIS2BRET.name: Francis II, Duke of Brittany
FRANCOIS2BRET.summary: A son of Richard of Brittany, he inherited the duchy after the lines of the relatives who had preceded him became extinct. He tried to preserve Brittany’s political autonomy against the French monarchy.
FRANCOIS2BRET.biography: A son of Richard of Brittany, he inherited the duchy after the lines of the relatives who had preceded him became extinct. He tried to preserve Brittany’s political autonomy against the French monarchy. His marriage to Margaret of Foix gave their daughter Anne, heiress to the duchy, a connection with the Pyrenean dynasties.

MIRCEACIOBAN.name: Mircea Ciobanul
MIRCEACIOBAN.summary: A son of Radu the Great, he ruled Wallachia in three separate periods interrupted by depositions and restorations. He married Chiajna, daughter of Petru Rareș of Moldavia.
MIRCEACIOBAN.biography: A son of Radu the Great, he ruled Wallachia in three separate periods interrupted by depositions and restorations. He married Chiajna, daughter of Petru Rareș of Moldavia. Their young son Petru succeeded him after his death. That continuity also depended on Ottoman intervention and struggles among the boyars.

MAGNUS4SUE.name: Magnus IV of Sweden
MAGNUS4SUE.summary: He gathered Sweden and Norway as a child through two different ways: Swedish choice and inheritance of his mother-grandfather Haakon V. His reign was known to be expanding towards Scania and to serious internal conflicts.
MAGNUS4SUE.biography: As a child he united Sweden and Norway by two different routes: election in Sweden and inheritance from his maternal grandfather Haakon V. His reign saw expansion toward Scania and serious internal conflicts. The transfer of Norwegian government to his son Haakon and his deposition in Sweden show that the union did not have an indivisible succession.

governmentNotes.La elección del hijo de Erik Magnusson d: The choice of Erik Magnusson gave a Swedish solution to the crisis following Birger's overthrow. It coincided with Norwegian inheritance but had a different basis.
governmentNotes.Heredó a su abuelo materno Haakon V a tr: He inherited his mother's grandfather Haakon V through Ingeborg of Norway. The king's minority demanded a regency government.

MARGAUST.name: Margaret of Austria
MARGAUST.summary: Governor of the House of Habsburg. Their life was connected with Low Countries.

FREDERICKHENRYORANGE.name: Frederick Henry, Prince of Orange
FREDERICKHENRYORANGE.summary: Son of William of Orange and Louise de Coligny, Frederick Henry succeeded his half-brother Maurice in 1625 as Prince of Orange and stadtholder of several provinces. He distinguished himself in siege warfare, notably at ’s-Hertogenbosch and Maastricht. His marriage to Amalia of Solms strengthened the court and the house’s alliances.

governmentNotes.Cargo provincial delegado por los Estado: Provincial office delegated by the States, with individually documented dates and jurisdictions. Its scope excludes hereditary sovereignty over the whole Republic and the Spanish provinces.

AGNESNAVFOIX.name: Agnes of Navarre, Countess of Foix
AGNESNAVFOIX.summary: Daughter of Philip of Évreux and Juana II of Navarre, married Gaston Fébus. She was the mother of the Count's legitimate son, also called Gaston.
AGNESNAVFOIX.biography: A daughter of Philip of Évreux and Joan II of Navarre, she married Gaston Fébus and was mother to the count’s legitimate son, also named Gaston. Her marriage connected Foix with Navarre, although the breakdown of the marriage and her son’s death prevented her descendants from continuing the male line.

governmentNotes.Año aproximado; la cifra no representa u: The figure does not represent an exact date.

BAGRAT3IMER.name: Bagrat III of Imereti
BAGRAT3IMER.summary: He tried to subdue the great western princes and extend his influence over Samtskhe. Ottoman intervention and rivalries with Mingrelia and Guria limited that policy. His daughter Tamar linked his house to the kings of Kartli.

LUARSAB1KARTLI.name: Luarsab I of Kartli
LUARSAB1KARTLI.summary: He defended Kartli's autonomy from his Safer campaigns. He died as a result of his battle with Garisi and his son Simon continued his resistance. The sources differ about some years of his reign, here from 1527 to 1556.

governmentNotes.También se documentan cronologías 1534–1: Chronologies 1534-1558 are also documented; 1527-1556 are adopted.

ROGERBERNARD2CASTEL.name: Roger Bernard II of Castellbó
ROGERBERNARD2CASTEL.summary: He continued the branch of Castellbó and was the father of Matthew and Elizabeth. Neither of the two inherited Fébus Gaston's Foix by direct descent: the link came from a collateral line. Its incorporation into the tree allows to follow that relationship without making the successor the son of the former ruler.

ALEX1GEO.name: Alexander I of Georgia
ALEX1GEO.summary: He tried to rebuild the kingdom after the Tamerlán campaigns and to recover rents and fortresses for the crown. He associated his children with power, a successor solution that also facilitated the subsequent division. He abdicated to enter a monastery.

MARIABORGCLEV.name: Mary of Burgundy, Duchess of Cleves
MARIABORGCLEV.summary: A daughter of John the Fearless and sister of Philip the Good, she married Adolf of Cleves. She was the mother of Catherine, wife of Arnold of Egmond. That line connected the dukes of Guelders with the Burgundian house that later intervened in its succession.

MARIACALABRIA.name: Maria of Calabria
MARIACALABRIA.summary: Noble of the House of Anjou. Their life was connected with Naples.

PETRURARESMOLD.name: Petru Rareș
PETRURARESMOLD.summary: Prince of Moldova and son of Stephen the Great. He tried to maintain an active policy between Poland, Hungary and the Ottoman Empire during a time when Moldovan autonomy was increasingly difficult to sustain.

MARIAHUNNAP.name: Mary of Hungary, Queen of Naples
MARIAHUNNAP.summary: Consort of the House of Árpád. Their life was connected with Naples, Hungary.

GIORGI7IMER.name: George VII of Imereti
GIORGI7IMER.summary: He regained the throne several times through changing alliances and Ottoman support. The interventions of the Gurieli and other nobles interrupted their authority. His sons Alexander V and George IX extended the royal branch during the 18th century.

ARTURO1BRET.name: Arthur I of Brittany
ARTURO1BRET.summary: The posthumous son of Godfredo of Brittany, he was a candidate for the angevine heritage in front of his uncle Juan Sin Tierra with the support of Felipe Augusto. Captured in Mirebeau in 1202, he disappeared in 1203; his death, attributed to John, precipitated the loss of Normandy.

governmentNotes.Proclamado duque en 1196 junto a su madr: Proclaimed duke alongside his mother in 1196. A rival of his uncle John for the Angevin inheritance, he was captured at Mirebeau in 1202 and disappeared in 1203.

BAGRAT5GEO.name: Bagrat V of Georgia
BAGRAT5GEO.summary: The invasion of Tamerlán culminated in the seizure of Tbilis and his captivity in 1386. He was released, but the Western campaigns and rebellions eroded the authority he had inherited. His sons George VII and Constantine I were kings.

MARGAUSTSAX.name: Margaret of Austria
MARGAUSTSAX.summary: Consort of the House of Habsburg. Their life was connected with Austria, Saxony.

JOHN6NASSAU.name: John VI of Nassau-Dillenburg
JOHN6NASSAU.summary: Count of Nassau, 1559–1606. Count of the House of Nassau.

VLADISLAVBOS.name: Vladislav of Bosnia
VLADISLAVBOS.summary: Brother of Stephen II and husband of Jelena Šubić, links the leading families of Bosnia and Croatia. His son Tvrtko inherited the banate as a young man. The participation of their parents in that first stage helps to understand that ownership and exercise of power were not always the same.

ISABELFARNESIO.name: Elisabeth Farnese
ISABELFARNESIO.summary: Consort of the House of Farnese. Their life was connected with Spain, Parma.

VALDEMAR4DIN.name: Valdemar IV of Denmark
VALDEMAR4DIN.summary: It restored much of the territorial power of the Danish monarchy after a phase of fragmentation and effort. His daughters Ingeborg and Margarita created two ways of dynastic continuity. The son of Margarita, Olaf, was elected king; the offspring of Ingeborg later contributed to Erik of Pomerania.

JOHNMONTPRET.name: John de Montfort
JOHNMONTPRET.summary: The son of Arturo II and Yolanda of Dreux, he fought the duchy to Juana of Penthièvre after the death of John III. His cause was supported by English and continued after his death, sustained by his wife and his son's supporters.
JOHNMONTPRET.biography: A son of Arthur II and Yolande of Dreux, he contested the duchy with Joan of Penthièvre after John III’s death. His cause received English support and continued after his death through his wife and his son’s supporters. His inclusion or exclusion from ducal lists explains some variations in the numbering of the dukes named John.

HUGOROGER3PALLARS.name: Hugh Roger III of Pallars
HUGOROGER3PALLARS.summary: Last count of Pallars. He led the pactista party in the Catalan civil war against John II, who held him in prison from 1466 to 1470, and was excluded from the capitulation of Pedralbes (1472). The troops of Fernando II conquered Pallars between 1484 and 1488, and in 1491 the county passed to the Cardona as a marquisate. Captured in Italy by the Grand Captain in 1503, he died in prison in the castle of Xàtiva in 1508.

governmentNotes.Conde hasta la guerra con Fernando II; l: Count till the war with Fernando II, with his confiscation sentence of 1488 and his county passed to the Cardonas in 1491.

GUILLERMOATENAS.name: William II of Athens
GUILLERMOATENAS.summary: Son of Frederick II of Sicily, he inherited the duchy of Athens in 1317 at the death of his brother Manfredo. Like him, he ruled from Sicily through vicars: his stepbrother Alfonso Fadrique conquered southern Thalia and formed in 1319 the duchy of Neopardia, united to that of Athens. He died in 1338.

governmentNotes.Sucedió a su hermano Manfredo. Gobernó e: He succeeded his brother Manfred. His half-brother Alfonso Fadrique governed the duchy as vicar-general.
governmentNotes.Ducado formado en 1319 con las conquista: Duchy of Styria formed in 1319 with the Conquests of Alfonso Fadrique in Thessaloniki.

GERALD8KILDARE.name: Gerald FitzGerald, VIII Count of Kildare
GERALD8KILDARE.summary: As a magnate and representative of the Crown, he made his family a central part of the Irish government. His victory at Knockdoe reinforced his ascending over Gaelic and Anglo-Irish rivals. He alternated conflicts and reconciliations with the Tudor.

ANDRO2.name: Andronikos II Palaiologos
ANDRO2.summary: I reduce the military resources of the Byzantine Empire in a context of serious fiscal difficulties. The arrival of the Catalan Company and the war with its grandson Andronikos III made the crisis worse.

PHIL2NEVERS.name: Philip II of Nevers
PHIL2NEVERS.summary: Count of Nevers, 1404–1415. Count of the House of Valois-Burgundy.

governmentNotes.Al acceder Juan sin Miedo al ducado en 1: When John without Fear reached his duchy in 1404 his brother Philip received Nevers and Rethel arrived in 1406.

ALFONSOBISCEGLIE.name: Alfonso of Aragon, Duke of Bisceglie
ALFONSOBISCEGLIE.summary: Duke of the House of Trastámara. Their life was connected with Naples, Bisseglie.

MATTHIEUFOIX.name: Matthew of Foix
MATTHIEUFOIX.summary: A member of the Castellbó branch, he succeeded Gaston Fébus in Foix and Béarn in 1391. His rule was brief and ended without descendants to continue his line. The inheritance passed to his sister Isabella, wife of Archambaud de Grailly, opening a new dynastic phase.

ALEXIOS3TREB.name: Alexios III of Trebizond
ALEXIOS3TREB.summary: He was granted power in 1349 and crowned in 1350. His long government strengthened religious patronage and the trade relations of the empire. Family connections with neighbouring powers colived with the competition of Italian merchants in the Black Sea.

governmentNotes.Acceso en 1349 y coronación en enero de: Access at 1349 and coronation at January 1350.

JOHN1AVES.name: John I of Avesnes
JOHN1AVES.summary: He defended the rights of the Avesnes over Henao in front of his half-brothers Dampierre. The arbitration of Louis IX supported a distribution of inheritance, but did not immediately eliminate conflicts. He died before his mother; his son John II continued the line of the condom.

governmentNotes.Derechos defendidos frente a Margarita y: Rights defended against Margarita and the Dampierre; it does not replace a peaceful and exclusive government.

OSHINARM.name: Oshin of Cilician Armenia
OSHINARM.summary: Brother of Hetum II, he obtained the crown after the murders of 1307. He tried to hold the kingdom between the Mamluk threat and the search for Western support. The discussions on religious union accompanied his foreign policy.

CATHCLEVEGUELD.name: Catherine of Cleves
CATHCLEVEGUELD.summary: She married Arnold of Egmond and was the mother of Adolfo and Mary of Guelders. Her family was involved in the conflict between father and son by the government of the duchy. For her mother, Catalina belonged to the family network of the Dukes of Burgundy.

FRIEDRICHAUGUSTANHALT.name: Frederick Augustus, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst
FRIEDRICHAUGUSTANHALT.summary: Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst from 1747 to 1793 and brother of Catherine II of Russia. His mother, Johanna Elisabeth of Holstein-Gottorp, acted as regent until 1752.

His mother exercised regency up to 1752. Jever's principality and inheritance did not amount to all Assyrian territories.

BASILEIOSTREB.name: Basil of Trebisonda
BASILEIOSTREB.summary: Son of Allejo II, took power in 1332. His offspring allows the imperial genealogy to continue until Alejo III, although this did not happen directly. The court passed through several changes of ruler between the two generations.

GABRIELESAL.name: Gabriel de Saluzzo
GABRIELESAL.summary: The last of the brothers who obtained the marquisate with French recognition, succeeded Francis in 1537. His government developed under a strong dependence on France.
GABRIELESAL.biography: The last of the brothers to hold the marquisate with French recognition, he succeeded Francis in 1537. His government operated under strong dependence on France. His death in 1548 opened the way for John Louis, shortly before the marquisate’s incorporation into the French monarchy.

JOANBEAUFORT.name: Joan Beaufort
JOANBEAUFORT.summary: A daughter of John of Gaunt and Katherine Swynford. Through her marriage to Ralph Neville she was the mother of Cecily Neville and Richard, Earl of Salisbury; her descendants connected the principal Yorkist leaders.

GUYPENTHIEVRE.name: Guy of Brittany
GUYPENTHIEVRE.summary: The son of Arthur II and Mary of Limoges, he was the brother of John III of Brittany and the father of Juana of Penthièvre. He died before the Duke.
GUYPENTHIEVRE.biography: A son of Arthur II and Marie of Limoges, he was brother to John III of Brittany and father to Joan of Penthièvre. He died before the duke. His daughter’s claim rested on his position within this branch, turning an apparently secondary relationship into one of the keys to the succession dispute of 1341.

JUANAPORTCAST.name: Joan of Portugal
JUANAPORTCAST.summary: Consort of the House of Aviz. Their life was connected with Castile, Portugal.

GUYCONSTCYP.name: Guy, Constable of Cyprus
GUYCONSTCYP.summary: Son of Hugo III and brother of Henry II, he served as a constable. He did not reign, but his son Hugo IV inherited the crown after Henry's death. His marriage linked him to the Beirut Ibelin.

ROGERBERNARD1CASTEL.name: Roger Bernard I of Castellbó
ROGERBERNARD1CASTEL.summary: Son of Gaston I of Foix, represents the family branch established in the province of Castellbó. This line retained its own position with respect to the main one.
ROGERBERNARD1CASTEL.biography: A son of Gaston I of Foix, he represented the branch established in the viscounty of Castellbó, which retained its own position alongside the main line. His descendants Matthew and Isabella eventually inherited Foix and Béarn, making this branch essential to understanding continuity after Gaston Fébus.

BEATRIZSICILIAPAL.name: Beatrice of Sicily
BEATRIZSICILIAPAL.summary: Consort of the House of Barcelona-Sicily. Their life was connected with Palatinate, Trinacria.

LEONORPOR.name: Eleanor of Portugal
LEONORPOR.summary: The daughter of King Duarte of Portugal and Leonor of Aragon, married Frederick III and was crowned Empress in Rome in 1452. Mother of Maximilian I, died in 1467.

ISABNAP.name: Isabella of Naples
ISABNAP.summary: Consort of the House of Trastámara. Their life was connected with Milan, Naples.

ALEX5IMER.name: Alexander V of Imereti
ALEX5IMER.summary: Its long political period included depositions and restorations, under Ottoman influence and with strong aristocratic intervention. He was the father of Solomon I and of Prince Archil, connecting the last two generations of unrighteous kings.

GEORGE1HESSEDARM.name: George I of Hesse-Darmstadt
GEORGE1HESSEDARM.summary: First landgrave of Hessen-Darmstadt. The division of Hesse became its own political actor, later closely linked to the houses of Brunswick and Hanover.

HENRY3MECK.name: Henry III of Mecklenburg
HENRY3MECK.summary: The son of Albert II of Mecklenburg and Euphemy of Sweden, and the brother of King Albert of Sweden. He married Ingeborg, daughter of Valdemar IV. The offspring of that marriage gathered ties with the three Nordic crowns; his grandson Erik of Pomerania was the crowned monarch in Kalmar.

governmentNotes.Gobernó con su hermano Magnus I tras la: He ruled with his brother Magnus I after his father's death.

NESTANKAKH.name: Nestan-Darejan of Kakheti
NESTANKAKH.summary: The daughter of Levan of Kakheti and wife of Simon I of Kartli. His family linked the two Eastern monarchies through their children and grandchildren; these marriages coexisted with political rivalries and with the intervention of Persia and the Ottomans.

ALB3BAV.name: Albert III of Bavaria-Munich
ALB3BAV.summary: Duke of Bavaria-Munich between 1438 and 1460. His union with Agnes Bernauer ended when his father, Duke Ernesto, drowned her on the Danube in 1435.

THOMAS7KILDARE.name: Thomas FitzGerald, Count of Kildare
THOMAS7KILDARE.summary: He sustained the Fitzgerald's position in the Irish government during the British dynastic wars. His family combined service to the Crown, alliances with Gaelic lineage and territorial domain. His son Gerald brought that influence to his apogee.

LUISBORGONAFRA.name: Louis, Duke of Burgundy
LUISBORGONAFRA.summary: Prince of the House of Bourbon. Their life was connected with France, Navarre.

LEONORMEDICI.name: Eleonora de’ Medici
LEONORMEDICI.summary: Consort of the House of Medici. Their life was connected with Mantua.

JAMES3SCOT.name: Section 3
JAMES3SCOT.summary: King of Scotland since 1460. He incorporated the Orcades and the Shetland for his marriage to Margarita of Denmark and died after the battle of Sauchieburn (1488) against noble rebels.

RAMONBERENGUER4PROV.name: Ramon Berenguer IV of Provence
RAMONBERENGUER4PROV.summary: Count of Provence, 1209–1245. Count of the House of Barcelona.

ISABELLACYPRUS.name: Isabella of Cyprus
ISABELLACYPRUS.summary: Princess of the House of Lusignan. Their life was connected with Cyprus, Jerusalem.

PIERRE1BRET.name: Peter of Dreux
PIERRE1BRET.summary: Known as Pierre Mauclerc, he belonged to Dreux's house and agreed to the Breton government for his marriage to Alix of Thouars. After her death, he exercised the regency of his son John I.
PIERRE1BRET.biography: Known as Pierre Mauclerc, he belonged to the House of Dreux and entered Breton government through his marriage to Alix of Thouars. After her death he served as regent for their son John I. His position toward the French and English crowns shifted during a career devoted to preserving broad ducal autonomy.

Government during the Juan I. minority

MARGABR.name: Margaret of Brabant
MARGABR.summary: Consort of the House of Brabant. Their life was connected with Germany, Luxembourg.

ENRIQ2BR.name: Henry II of Brabante
ENRIQ2BR.summary: Duke of Brabant, 1235–1248. Duke of the House of Brabant.

FERNPORTVISEU.name: Ferdinand of Portugal
aliases: Ferdinand of Portugal, duque de Viseu
FERNPORTVISEU.summary: Son of King Duarte, he was Duke of Viseu and Beja and heir of the throne during the minority of his brother Alfonso V. Married to his cousin Beatriz, he died in Setúbal in 1470; his younger son reigned as Manuel I.

RENEAFRA.name: Renée of France
RENEAFRA.summary: Consort of the House of Valois-Orléans. Their life was connected with France, Ferrara.

BEATRIZNAP.name: Beatrice of Naples
BEATRIZNAP.summary: Consort of the House of Trastámara. Their life was connected with Hungary.

MAGNUS2MECK.name: Magnus II of Mecklenburg
MAGNUS2MECK.summary: Duke of Mecklenburg, 1477–1503. Duke of the House of Mecklenburg.

PIERRE2BRET.name: Peter II of Brittany
PIERRE2BRET.summary: He succeeded his brother Francis I in the duchy. Because he had no son to continue his line, government later passed to his uncle Arthur of Richemont. His place in the family tree shows a succession through brothers and uncles before Francis II inherited through another Montfort branch.

BIANCAMONSAB.name: Blanche of Montferrat
BIANCAMONSAB.summary: Daughter of William VIII of Monferrato, married Charles I of Savoy. After the death of the Duke, he took over the regency of her son Carlos Juan Amadeo and defended her authority before the relatives of the house.
BIANCAMONSAB.biography: A daughter of William VIII of Montferrat, she married Charles I of Savoy. After his death she served as regent for their son Charles John Amadeus and defended her authority against relatives of the house. When the child died in 1496, the duchy passed to Philip II. Blanche belonged to the Palaiologan house of Montferrat, not to the marquesses of Saluzzo.

PHILIPANTARM.name: Philip of Antioch, King of Armenia
aliases: Philip of Antioch, King of Armenia
PHILIPANTARM.summary: Son of Bohemond IV, he gained the crown through his marriage to Isabella. Opposition among part of the Armenian nobility to his policies ended in his deposition and imprisonment. His fall opened the way for Isabella’s marriage to Hethum.

HENRYANTIOCH.name: Henry of Antioch
HENRYANTIOCH.summary: Son of Bohemundo IV and husband of Elizabeth of Cyprus. His son Hugo III inherited the Cypriot crown by the mother line, retained the name Lusignan and brought to his descendants the genealogy of the princes of Antioch.

KETEVANMARTYR.name: Ketevan of Kakheti
KETEVANMARTYR.summary: Widow of David I, defended the rights of her son Teimuraz and intervened in the Kakhetin government. She was held hostage in Persia and was executed after refusing to convert to Islam. Her religious memory transcended Georgia through missionary testimonies.

INGEBORGNORUEGA.name: Ingeborg of Norway
INGEBORGNORUEGA.summary: Daughter of Haakon V and Euphemy. Her marriage to Erik Magnusson linked Norway to the Swedish house of Bjälbo. Her son Magnus inherited Norway and was elected king of Sweden in 1319. Ingeborg intervened in minority politics, although the councils of both kingdoms then limited their authority.

ERNEST1.name: Ernest I of Austria
ERNEST1.summary: Duke of Inner Austria, 1406–1424. Duke of the House of Habsburg.

governmentNotes.Duque de Estiria, Carintia y Carniola, b: Duke of Styria, Carintia and Carniola, base of the Habsburg Styria line.

ISABBAVIERA.name: Isabeau of Bavaria
ISABBAVIERA.summary: Consort of the House of Wittelsbach. Their life was connected with France.

SOFIAMAGDALENADIN.name: Sophia Magdalene of Denmark
SOFIAMAGDALENADIN.summary: Consort of the House of Oldenburg. Their life was connected with Denmark, Sweden.

CATAUSTRIAPOL.name: Catherine of Austria
CATAUSTRIAPOL.summary: Consort of the House of Habsburg. Their life was connected with Poland, Austria.

EDUVK.name: Hedwig of Kalisz
EDUVK.summary: Consort of the House of Piast. Their life was connected with Poland.

MARIEELEONORECLEVES.name: Maria Eleanor of Cleves
MARIEELEONORECLEVES.summary: Consort of the House of La Marck. Their life was connected with Cleves, Prussia.

FRANCISCOVENDOME.name: Francis of Bourbon-Vendôme
FRANCISCOVENDOME.summary: Count of Vendôme, 1477–1495. Count of the House of Bourbon.

LUIS1FLA.name: Louis I of Flanders
LUIS1FLA.summary: Count of Flanders, 1322–1346. Count of the House of Dampierre.

governmentNotes.Luis heredó de su abuelo Roberto III: su: Luis inherited from his grandfather Robert III: his father, Louis of Nevers, had died shortly before. A genealogical generation does not amount to an intermediate government here.

MAGNUS3SUE.name: Magnus III of Sweden
MAGNUS3SUE.summary: Magnus Ladulås, king of Sweden since 1275 after deposing his brother Valdemar. It strengthened the real authority and granted tax privileges to the nobility serving on horseback.

SHANEONEILL.name: Shane O'Neill
SHANEONEILL.summary: He defended his election as head of the O'Neill and his successor system at Tyrone County. He alternated war and negotiations with Elizabeth I and disputed the predominance of Northern Ireland to other Gaelic houses.

BELA4.name: Béla IV of Hungary
BELA4.summary: After the Hungarian defeat of Mohi in front of the Mongols, he promoted the reconstruction of the kingdom and the building of stone fortresses. He is reminded of this work as a second founder of Hungary.

ROB3FLAND.name: Robert III of Flanders
ROB3FLAND.summary: He succeeded Guy of Dampierre as Count of Flanders. His rule belongs to the difficult relationship among comital power, the Flemish cities and the French monarchy. Because his son Louis of Nevers died before him, the succession passed to his grandson Louis I.

governmentNotes.Roberto III sucedió a su padre Guido. La: Robert III succeeded his father Guy. The consequences of the conflict with the French crown constrained the exercise of comital authority.

JUANORLEANS.name: John of Orléans
JUANORLEANS.summary: Count of Angulem, 1407–1467. Count of the House of Valois-Orléans.

BEATFLAHOL.name: Beatrice de Flanders
BEATFLAHOL.summary: Daughter of Guy of Dampierre, married Floris V of the Netherlands. She was the mother of John I, the last Dutch count of that male line. Her marriage linked two neighbouring houses whose heritage would end up gathering long after under the Dukes of Burgundy.

ANNECLEVES.name: Anne of Cleves
ANNECLEVES.summary: Consort of the House of La Marck. Their life was connected with Cleves, England.

LOUISEGBDEN.name: Louise of Great Britain
LOUISEGBDEN.summary: Consort of the House of Hanover. Their life was connected with England, Denmark.

MICHAEL9PALA.name: Michael IX Palaiologos
MICHAEL9PALA.summary: Son of Andrónico II, associated with the throne as co-emperor. He led campaigns against the Turks and the Catalan Company without success, and died before his father in 1320.

BLANCAFRANCIAORLEANS.name: Blanche of France, Duchess of Orléans
